reports.title: Select Water Solutions Announces Third Quarter 2026 Financial, Operational and Strategic Updates

lines: “Taking into consideration the divestment and deconsolidation of Peak Rentals and a partial quarter contribution from Pilot Water, we anticipate Adjusted EBITDA in the fourth quarter growing to an estimated $95 - $100 million.

Additionally, as we begin integrating the combined asset base and finish out Pilot Water’s ongoing capital projects during the fourth quarter, we now anticipate net capital expenditures for 2026 of approximately $300 – $310 million.

Looking ahead, the Company anticipates Water Infrastructure revenues of $150 - $160 million in the fourth quarter of 2026, driven by a partial quarter contribution from Pilot Water, with gross margins before D&A in the 52% – 56% range in the fourth quarter of 2026.

Normalizing for the divestment of Peak Rentals, which contributed approximately 21% of the segment’s revenues year-to-date, the Company anticipates typical fourth quarter seasonality for the segment resulting in mid single-digit percent declines sequentially for the remaining segment.

For the fourth quarter of 2026, the Company anticipates revenues of $75 – $80 million, driven by the timing of key customer activity levels and fourth quarter seasonality, with gross margins before D&A remaining steady in the 17% – 18% range for the segment.

desk.headline: Revenue up 28% to $412m, beat; Q4 adjusted EBITDA guided to $95-100m with Pilot Water added

other.label: Water Infrastructure gross margin before D&A

results: Revenue rose 28% to $412m, above the $396m estimate; net income rose to $22.9m and diluted EPS to $0.16 from $0.03.
Water Infrastructure revenue hit a record $110m (+40%) as produced-water volumes rose to 1.7m bbl/d, with a 57.2% margin before D&A.
Water Services grew 7% from Q2 to $212m, while Chemical Technologies dipped to $90m, at the top of its guided range.
Adjusted EBITDA rose 57% to $93.5m; SG&A included $7.4m of deal costs.
Select sold 55% of Peak Rentals for about $76.8m in late September and, after quarter-end, closed the Pilot Water purchase, funded by $900m of 7.625% notes due 2034.

guidance.summary: For Q4 Select expects adjusted EBITDA of $95-100m, including part of a quarter from Pilot Water and without Peak Rentals. It now expects 2026 net capex of about $300-310m; the release does not give the earlier figure.

points: Management said Pilot Water is tracking its 2026 targets of $250-270m revenue and $100-110m adjusted EBITDA, and sees $120-130m EBITDA in 2027.
Pilot adds about 900,000 bbl/d of disposal capacity; management now hopes to bring some revenue synergies forward into 2027.
Deconsolidating Peak Rentals is expected to take $7-10m out of Q4 EBITDA; Select keeps a 45% stake.
Pro forma leverage is about 2.0x net debt to EBITDA; full 2027 guidance comes with year-end results, with capex starting near 2026 levels.
Maintenance capex is expected to rise to $80-90m a year on the larger asset base.
